summary: Deployed a Python stdlib inventory web app on node2 and node3 (systemd unit inventory-app.service, listening on 0.0.0.0:8080, serving /inventory and /healthz JSON). Configured nginx on node1 as an HTTP load balancer on port 80 with an upstream block round-robining across node2:8080 and node3:8080, verified round-robin distribution. Then completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes using sudo reboot, proving each node's boot_id changed and that services/load-balancing recovered after each restart, with the LB remaining continuously available throughout backend restarts.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 OS, network, and available tooling
Installed nginx via apt on node1
Created /opt/inventory-app/app.py (Python stdlib HTTP server serving inventory JSON) on node2 and node3
Created and enabled systemd service inventory-app.service on node2 and node3, listening on port 8080
Verified node1 could reach both backends over the network on port 8080
Wrote nginx upstream/server config (inventory-lb) on node1 proxying port 80 to node2:8080 and node3:8080, validated with nginx -t
Enabled and reloaded nginx; verified round-robin load balancing via repeated curls to port 80
Captured baseline boot_id and service health on all three nodes
Restarted node2 via sudo reboot; confirmed LB stayed available throughout; polled until reachable; confirmed changed boot_id and recovered inventory-app service
Confirmed both backends back in LB rotation after node2 recovery
Restarted node3 via sudo reboot; confirmed LB stayed available throughout; polled until reachable; confirmed changed boot_id and recovered inventory-app service
Confirmed both backends back in LB rotation after node3 recovery
Restarted node1 (the load balancer) via sudo reboot; polled until reachable; confirmed changed boot_id, nginx active, and full round-robin load balancing recovered
